summary: Minimum number of meeting rooms needed for a set of time intervals.
mainInsight: Sort by start time and keep a min-heap of the end times of rooms in use. For each meeting, free the room whose end time is <= its start (pop), then push this meeting's end. The heap size at its maximum is the answer. Alternative: sort starts and ends separately and sweep.

approaches.name: Min-heap of end times
approaches.summary: Pop the earliest end if it is <= the start, push the new end.

commonMistakes: Using < instead of <= when freeing a room
Returning the final heap size instead of the maximum

promptVariants: Why is sorting by start time necessary?
What does the heap size represent after processing a meeting?
cards.answer: Processing meetings in start order means each new meeting only has to compare with the room that frees up earliest (the heap root). After handling a meeting, the heap size is the number of rooms occupied at that start time, and the maximum over all meetings is the answer.
cards.explanation: Without sorting by start you cannot reuse rooms greedily.
